decisions.reason: As a newly launched core door-hardware family that fits the firm's established architectural system business, its still-uncertain early performance is likely to be tolerated within normal portfolio slack unless results clearly fall below aspiration.

This mitred handle family is close to the firm's core design-and-specification capabilities, so management would likely keep it while learning about market acceptance rather than redeploy resources immediately.

A multifunctional door lever aligns well with the firm's accessibility and integrated-solution strategy, making it likely to be retained as a promising extension even if first-year evidence is limited.

Because it is another adjacent handle line within the firm's broad certified range, management would usually continue it for another year unless sales feedback proved distinctly worse than comparable launches.
Its dedicated presentation and German Design Award signal above-aspiration external validation, so there is little behavioral reason to drop it in the next year.

A finish option is easier to rationalize than a full product family if uptake disappoints, but it still supports the firm's design-led one-stop offering and would likely be kept while demand is assessed.
